WoW: Forever

Protection Paladin

Shield tanking that generates threat from Holy damage rather than weapon damage, which makes it the only tank in the game that gears for Spell Power.

WoW: Forever · Tank · Updated October 8, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70245 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Protection build has been tested. Talent tiers unlock at levels 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40.

No source has posted a level 30 build either. The cap only reached 30 on October 1, and none of the three sites has published one since. So the level 30 line below extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs; no guide recommends it.

What Protection is for

Taking several enemies at once, and taunting without spending a talent point. Seal of FurySeal of FuryLevel 10 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secFills you with divine fury for 30 sec, causing melee attacks to deal an additional 6 Holy damage. While a shield is equipped, each attack also grants an absorb shield equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Unleashing this Seal's energy inflicts23 Holy damage to an enemy and taunts the target to attack you for 4 sec. is available from level 10, and judging it taunts: that is baseline, not a talent. ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. amplified by Righteous FuryRighteous FuryLevel 16 · Spell · HolyCastInstantDuration1800 secIncreases the threat generated by your Holy attacks by 60%. Lasts 1800 sec. puts threat on everything in the ring, which is why Spell Power leads your stat priority.

You can safely pull several enemies and grind them down. Mana is what limits you.

Forever nerfed the thing this spec used to be good at. Protection Paladin's dungeon levelling rested on ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec., its one source of damage to a whole pull. Forever cut dungeon experience hard, and one published guide calls that out as hurting this spec more than any other. The October 1 build went further, cutting the extra experience on dungeon quests by 50% as a deliberate reduction in levelling speed.

No source publishes a levelling score for any Paladin spec. That experience cut and the guide's warning about it are what the sources say on levelling here.

Swapping seals removes your taunt (ours, not a source's). Do not press it for damage.

Stat priority

Spell Power, then Hit, Stamina, Defense, Armor, Block, Intellect, Strength, Agility.

Spell Power first genuinely is correct here. In Forever a Paladin's threat is Holy damage: Seal of FurySeal of FuryLevel 10 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secFills you with divine fury for 30 sec, causing melee attacks to deal an additional 6 Holy damage. While a shield is equipped, each attack also grants an absorb shield equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Unleashing this Seal's energy inflicts23 Holy damage to an enemy and taunts the target to attack you for 4 sec., ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. and Holy StrikeHoly StrikeLevel 6 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost5 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown10 sec cooldownAn instant strike that causes 25% weapon damage plus an additional 12 as Holy damage., all amplified by Righteous FuryRighteous FuryLevel 16 · Spell · HolyCastInstantDuration1800 secIncreases the threat generated by your Holy attacks by 60%. Lasts 1800 sec.. Seal of Fury's absorb is worth half of that damage again. Take mail over leather where the stats are close, and carry a shield, which Seal of Fury's absorb requires.

Righteous FuryRighteous FuryLevel 16 · Spell · HolyCastInstantDuration1800 secIncreases the threat generated by your Holy attacks by 60%. Lasts 1800 sec.'s multiplier moved in the September 24 build, and Blizzard's own wording does not parse. The note reads "Righteous Fury: Holy threat increase increased to 60% (was 90%)". But 60% is lower than 90%, so the verb and the numbers contradict each other. Both figures are Blizzard's, and that post does not settle which way the multiplier moved, so read it as an apparent slip rather than a published buff or nerf. The case for Spell Power holds either way: the amplifier multiplies Holy damage whichever number is live.

Leave spell power weapons alone below 20. Wowhead flags a trap here: a weapon with a heavy spell power roll carries roughly a 25% melee damage penalty, and you do not have the spell-power talents yet to make that trade pay off. A plain melee weapon out-damages it until you hit 20.

At level 60

Unknown, and one open question is specific: whether a 4-second conditional taunt can hold a raid boss. The ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. bug Wowhead reported is fixed: it left targets inside the ring not taking its full damage, worst near the edge. Blizzard's September 24 build repaired Consecration's failure to apply its increased damage effect to some targets, its inconsistent Z axis, and a case where it pulled targets vertically above or below the caster.
